Hi Marta — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to provide a compact evidence packet. High-level answers are below and we'll attach the artifacts in a follow-up from Marissa (security ops).

Summary (short):
- Platform KEKs: rotated automatically by the control-plane agent every 90 days; emergency rotation can be triggered by the Ops on-call with an approved change ticket. Rotations produce an immutable audit record captured in the rotation-log service.
- Tenant KEKs (BYOK): customers can schedule automated rotations or request one-off rotations via the private control plane; when BYOK is enabled the customer holds key material and Redwood records a wrap/transfer event but does not export plaintext.
- Wrap metadata: we only share descriptive metadata (wrapped_key_id, wrap_algorithm, key_uri, timestamp, operator-id, envelope_version). No ciphertext or raw key material in transit.

I'll ring Marissa to assemble the files you asked for. Expect a link + three attachments from us within the next business day.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
